copy.blurb:
FIFA World Cup 2026 on Friday, evening UTC kickoff, brings Norway and France together. The Desk's read disagrees with the market on the France side, by +17.7pp — and that disagreement is the Pick.

On Elo, France comes in 270 points ahead — Norway at 1760, France at 2030. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Norway to win at 15%, the draw at 14%, and France to win at 71%. The Desk publishes a three-way read against the same W/D/L resolution Polymarket and Kalshi settle on — not a scoreline guess. France sits at 71% of the mass.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Norway to win at 20%, the draw at 24%, and France to win at 54%. On the France side specifically the market reads 54%, which prices out at American odds of −115. Compared against the model's 71%, that's the +17.7pp gap the Pick rests on.

Pick gate is a lower-bound check, not the point estimate. A 100-sample bootstrap perturbs the Elo prior (±20), the host bonus (±15), and the altitude bonus (±10), then reads the 5th-percentile probability back out. On the France side that lower bound is 64% — +10.3pp clear of the market's 54%, comfortably past our +3pp threshold. The engine isn't arguing reputation, recency, or narrative. It's reading the underlying numbers and finding France priced shorter on the market than the prior supports — that's the disagreement.

This number will move. The confirmed starting eleven, fitness news, weather at the venue, and any tournament suspension carried in from previous matches all feed back into the prior. With kickoff 35 days out, the refresh is weekly until we cross five days, then daily, then hourly inside the final day. A wide Pick can collapse into a Pass if news moves enough of the read. Editorial analysis only — Odds Primer does not place trades and does not recommend a wager.

copy.summary: On every meaningful read, France look stronger here than Polymarket has them. Model 71% vs market 54% — a +17.7pp gap on the favourite side.
